newsitem.title: TOGO: Togo's premier sees 7.1 percent growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Togo's premier sees 7.1 percent growth in 1997.

text.p: Togo's economy is expected to grow by 7.1 percent in 1997, up slightly from the 7.0 percent recorded in 1996, Prime Minister Kwassi Klutse said.
"After falling 18.4 percent in 1993, gross domestic product has increased constantly in recent years and is stabilising," Klutse told Reuters in an interview last week.
Another sign of recovery is the growing balance of payments surplus, which reached 13.2 billion CFA francs ($23.3 million) in 1996, up from 1.5 billion in 1995.
Togo's external debt stood at 746 billion CFA francs at the end of 1996, and its internal debt -- money owed by the state and state firms -- amounted to 204 billion.
However, Klutse said the government intended to pay off some 65 billion of the internal debt this year, including seven billion that would go towards pay owed to civil servants.
Klutse said the pick-up in the economy owed much to increases in production of commodities such as coffee, cocoa, cotton and phosphate, which is its main export.
Togo has entered into a three-year structural adjustment agreement with the International Monetary Fund for 1997-99 and plans to privatise around 20 state companies.
